content:
A woman dubbed "Mother of the Year" by the San Francisco Giants broadcast team in a viral video has stepped forward to defend her husband after the clip sparked widespread online criticism of him.

The incident happened last Tuesday, when the couple brought their daughter to San Francisco's Oracle Park. The woman was seen carrying a baby in one arm and several food containers down the stairs back to her seat, while her husband appeared in no rush and even started having food, leaving the mother to handle everything on her own. The commentators immediately crowned her "Super Mom."

Commentators Duane Kuiper and Mike Krukow heaped praise on the woman's multitasking abilities, calling her an "Olympic gold medalist" and "Mother of the Year," and portrayed the father in the frame as a cold villain who only cared about getting ketchup. Netizens piled on in agreement.

So Erika, who declined to reveal her surname, decided to fight back, throwing a sharp curveball in response.

In a post published on Substack on September 25, she wrote: "Millions of viewers watched me carrying my daughter and food back to my seat at a San Francisco Giants game, and they crowned me 'Mother of the Year' while hurling countless vile names at my husband. Some even sent me private messages or posted TikTok videos telling me I should leave him."

She continued: "My name is Erika, our daughter is Anastasia, and my husband is Ramses. Before you pass judgment on our marriage, please hear from the person you've been condemning."

Erika went on the offensive in her post, writing:

"Ramses is an amazing husband and an even better father. We've been together for nine years and are currently raising two children under the age of two together. I know exactly how he treats me, how much he loves our kids, and what he does for our family. A conversation that the audience couldn't hear became the basis for millions of people to make assumptions about our lives."

She also explained that Ramses had originally offered to hold their daughter so she could use the restroom (and then go get food), and he had asked whether she wanted to eat first and whether she needed him to carry the containers. She turned him down each time, and he was feeling down that evening over the death of a close friend.

"In our marriage, whoever needs support, the other steps in. That night, I chose to take care of him. The camera captured one moment of me doing something for my husband, but couldn't show the countless times he has done the same for me."
